prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single definitive “best” HVAC company for everyone in Houston — the right choice depends on your exact location, the make/model of your system, how quickly you need service, your budget, and whether you want a warranty/maintenance plan. I can, however, help you find a highly qualified local tech. To get the best result I need your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and whether this is an emergency repair or a routine fix/replacement.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick checklist and process you can use to pick a top HVAC company in Houston:

What to look for
- Proper licensing and insurance (TX HVAC license / TDLR registration and liability insurance).
- NATE-certified technicians or manufacturer-specific certifications.
- Good recent reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor and a solid BBB rating.
- Clear, written estimates that list parts, labor, and any diagnostic fee.
- A parts and labor warranty (ask length and what’s covered).
- Availability for emergency or after-hours service if you need it.
- Transparent pricing and willingness to show the failed parts or explain the issue.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I have your license number?
- How quickly can you get a technician to my home?
- Do you charge a diagnostic fee and is it applied to the repair?
- What warranty do you offer on parts and labor?
- Do your technicians carry parts for my brand/model, or would you need to order?

Typical repair-cost ranges (rough guide)
- Minor repairs (thermostat, capacitors, sensors): ~$100–$400
- Moderate repairs (run capacitor, contactor, refrigerant leak repair): ~$300–$900
- Major repairs (compressor, coil, major refrigerant work): ~$800–$2,500+  
(Actual prices vary a lot by system, brand, and extent of the work.)

Where to check ratings
- Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi (HomeAdvisor), BBB, and local Facebook community groups.

If you want, tell me:
- your ZIP code,
- make/model of the AC (if known),
- whether it’s urgent,
and I’ll recommend 3–5 well-reviewed HVAC companies in your immediate area and what to expect from each.
